tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with a new column label and a specified fill_value.
tests.post_condition: The new column is filled with the specified fill_value.
tests.unique_reason: No other test verifies that fill_value is applied to missing column labels.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation states fill_value applies to missing values, including columns. This is falsifiable if fill_value is ignored for new columns.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame with a monotonically increasing index is reindexed with method='bfill'.
tests.post_condition: Gaps in the new index are filled with the next valid observation backward.
tests.unique_reason: No other test specifically demonstrates the backward fill behavior with a monotonic index.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation describes 'backfill / bfill: Use next valid observation to fill gap.' This is falsifiable if backward fill does not use the next observation.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with method='nearest'.
tests.post_condition: Values are filled from the nearest index position.
tests.unique_reason: No other test specifically checks the nearest neighbor fill behavior.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation states 'nearest: Use nearest valid observations to fill gap.' This is falsifiable if a non-nearest value is used.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame with existing NaN values is reindexed with a fill method.
tests.post_condition: The pre-existing NaN values are not filled.
tests.unique_reason: No other test verifies that fill methods do not alter existing NaN values in the source DataFrame.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation explicitly notes 'the NaN value present in the original DataFrame will not be filled by any of the value propagation schemes.' This is falsifiable if pre-existing NaN is filled.

tests.pre_condition: A MultiIndex DataFrame is reindexed at a specific level with a new level value not present.
tests.post_condition: New rows for the new level value have NaN values.
tests.unique_reason: No other test verifies NaN addition for new level values in MultiIndex reindexing.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation implies that reindexing at a level adds NaN for missing level values, similar to standard reindexing. This is falsifiable if new level values are not handled with NaN.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with tolerance and method='nearest'.
tests.post_condition: Labels within the tolerance are matched and filled.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks that tolerance allows matches within a specified distance.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation describes tolerance as 'Maximum distance between original and new labels for inexact matches.' This is falsifiable if within-tolerance labels are not matched.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with tolerance, and labels are outside the tolerance.
tests.post_condition: Labels outside the tolerance receive NaN.
tests.unique_reason: No other test verifies that labels outside tolerance get NaN.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation implies that matches beyond tolerance result in NaN. This is falsifiable if outside-tolerance labels are filled.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame with a non-monotonic index is reindexed with a fill method.
tests.post_condition: An error is raised.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks that fill methods require a monotonic index.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation warns 'this is only applicable to DataFrames/Series with a monotonically increasing/decreasing index.' This is falsifiable if no error is raised for non-monotonic indices.

tests.pre_condition: A MultiIndex DataFrame is reindexed at a specific level with existing level values.
tests.post_condition: Rows with matching level values are preserved.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks reindexing at a MultiIndex level with existing values.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation states 'level int or name: Broadcast across a level, matching Index values on the passed MultiIndex level.' This is falsifiable if matching rows are not preserved.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with an identical index to the original.
tests.post_condition: All values in the DataFrame are unchanged.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks that reindexing with the same index leaves values intact.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation suggests that reindexing with an equivalent index reproduces the data. This is falsifiable if values are altered unnecessarily.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with method='backfill' and method='bfill'.
tests.post_condition: Both method calls produce the same result.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks that 'backfill' is an alias for 'bfill'.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation lists 'backfill / bfill' as synonyms in the method parameter. This is falsifiable if the aliases are not implemented consistently.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with only a subset of the original column labels.
tests.post_condition: Columns not in the new list are absent from the resulting DataFrame.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks that reindexing with fewer columns drops the omitted columns.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation for reindexing columns implies that columns not specified are dropped; examples demonstrate this. This is falsifiable if removed columns persist.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with arbitrary new labels.
tests.post_condition: The result is always a DataFrame instance.
tests.unique_reason: No other test solely asserts the return type of the reindex method.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation lists 'Returns: DataFrame.' This is falsifiable as an incorrect implementation might return a different type.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame with a monotonically increasing index is reindexed with method='ffill'.
tests.post_condition: Gaps in the new index are filled with the last valid observation forward.
tests.unique_reason: No other test specifically demonstrates the forward fill behavior with a monotonic index.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation describes 'pad / ffill: Propagate last valid observation forward to next valid.' This is falsifiable if forward fill does not propagate correctly.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with new row labels and a specified fill_value.
tests.post_condition: The missing row labels are filled with the specified fill_value.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks that a custom fill_value is applied to missing row labels.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation states 'fill_value scalar, default np.nan: Value to use for missing values.' This is falsifiable if fill_value is ignored for missing rows.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed using the axis=0 parameter with labels.
tests.post_condition: The result is equal to reindexing using the index keyword with the same labels.
tests.unique_reason: No other test verifies the equivalence between axis-style and keyword-style calling conventions for rows.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation indicates equivalence between axis and keyword parameters for rows. This is falsifiable if inconsistencies arise.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with method='pad' and method='ffill'.
tests.post_condition: Both method calls produce the same result.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks that 'pad' is an alias for 'ffill'.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation lists 'pad / ffill' as synonyms in the method parameter. This is falsifiable if the aliases are not implemented consistently.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with new row labels that include labels not present in the original index.
tests.post_condition: The resulting DataFrame has NaN values for the missing row labels.
tests.unique_reason: No other test specifically covers missing row labels receiving NaN by default without a custom fill_value.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation states 'Places NA/NaN in locations having no value in the previous index.' This is falsifiable as an incorrect implementation might place non-NaN values.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed simultaneously with new index and column labels.
tests.post_condition: The shape of the resulting DataFrame matches (len(new_index), len(new_columns)).
tests.unique_reason: No other test directly asserts the shape after reindexing with both new index and columns.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation implies that reindexing with new index and columns results in a DataFrame with the specified dimensions. This is falsifiable if the shape does not correspond.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with a subset of the original index labels.
tests.post_condition: Values for labels present in both the old and new index are preserved exactly.
tests.unique_reason: No other test specifically targets preservation of values for existing labels during reindexing with a subset.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation implies that reindexing retains data for existing labels; examples show preserved values. This is falsifiable if values are altered.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed using the axis='columns' parameter with labels.
tests.post_condition: The result is equal to reindexing using the columns keyword with the same labels.
tests.unique_reason: No other test verifies the equivalence between axis-style and keyword-style calling conventions for columns.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation notes 'DataFrame.reindex supports two calling conventions' and shows equivalence. This is falsifiable if the two conventions produce different results.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with a limit parameter on fills.
tests.post_condition: Filling stops after the specified number of consecutive positions.
tests.unique_reason: No other test verifies the limit parameter's effect on consecutive fills.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation states 'limit int, default None: Maximum number of consecutive elements to forward or backward fill.' This is falsifiable if limit is ignored.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with the same index as the original.
tests.post_condition: The result is a new DataFrame object and not the same object as the original.
tests.unique_reason: No other test checks object identity after reindexing with the same index.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation specifies 'this method always returns a new object using a lazy copy mechanism.' This is falsifiable if reindexing returns a view instead of a new object.

tests.pre_condition: A DataFrame is reindexed with a column label not present in the original columns.
tests.post_condition: The new column is filled with NaN values by default.
tests.unique_reason: No other test covers NaN filling for new column labels without a fill_value.
tests.valid_reason: Documentation examples show new columns get NaN when reindexing columns. This is falsifiable if new columns receive non-NaN values.
